title: Mordheim KB catalogue — catalog/campaign/trading-post.yaml
description: The market: base price, availability and restrictions of every tradable item, plus the purchase options a few of them carry (a brace, a first free dagger). It is the only source of market price, rarity and post-battle availability — `bands/*/equipment-access.yaml` says who may select an item when creating the warband and never repeats the market price, and a confirmed difference is recorded there as a `price_override`, not as a second implicit price here.

items.description: One entry per tradable item. The entry keeps a campaign id of its own and points at the canonical record through `item_id`; the item definition is never duplicated.

effect_ids.description: Effects of the market a warband's own special rules may modify.

id.description: Stable campaign id of the `campaign.trading-post.*` family; a purchase option gets an explicit child id such as `campaign.trading-post.pistol.brace`.

price.description: The published market price, or `null` when the source lists the item without printing a market price.

restrictions.description: Who may buy the item. An empty list is the declared convention for `no restriction`.

purchase_options.description: Alternative ways of buying the same item, e.g. a brace of two or a first free dagger.

price.description: A published market price. It is either a fixed amount with an optional variable surcharge, or a multiplier applied to the record being upgraded.

base_gc.description: Fixed part of the price, in gold crowns.

multiplier.description: Multiple of the base price of the record being upgraded, e.g. Gromril Weapon at 4x. Used instead of `base_gc`, not next to it.

per.description: Unit of sale the price applies to. `pair` prices the brace as a whole.

variable_cost.description: A rolled surcharge on top of the base price, as the source prints it: `10 + 1D6 gc` is `{ dice: { count: 1, sides: 6 } }` on a `base_gc: 10`.

multiplier.description: Multiple applied to the rolled amount, e.g. `D6 x 25`.

availability.description: How the item is obtained after a battle.

kind.description: `common` is always available and needs no test; `rare` requires a rarity test against `rarity` (see `trading-and-rarity.yaml`); `not_sold` is listed by the source but not on the market.

rarity.description: The `Rare N` value a rarity test must reach. Declared exactly when the item is `rare`, and read from here by the rarity rule instead of being repeated in it.

restriction.description: A typed buying restriction. `condition` and `profile_only` carry the source wording in `note` because the restriction is editorial prose, not a rule the applications evaluate yet. A warband restriction names either the individual bands (`band_ids`) or the shared groups (`groups`) it applies to, never both.

purchase_option.description: An alternative way of buying the item.

id.description: Child id of the entry, e.g. `campaign.trading-post.pistol.brace`.

quantity.description: How many units the option buys at once.
